test_title: SSC CGL Tier 2 Quant Previous Year Paper (Held On: 8 Aug 2022)
subject: general
question: The height of a cylinder is 6 cm more than the radius of its base. If its radius is 14 cm, then what will be volume of this cylinder ? (use π = 22/7)
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Given: Radius (r) = 14 cm.

Height (h) = Radius + 6 = 14 + 6 = 20 cm.

Volume = πr²h = (22/7) × 14 × 14 × 20.

Volume = 44 × 14 × 20 = 12320 cm³.

**∴ The correct answer is 12320 cm³.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of base (r) = 14 cm

Height of cylinder (h) = r + 6 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of Cylinder (V) = π × r² × h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f966b3d8ba1fbc9385ffe0d482bba99f4acee641338e8b7d8ff5145a08630a13.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Radius (r) = 14 cm

⇒ Height (h) = 14 + 6 = 20 cm

⇒ Volume (V) = (22/7) × 14 × 14 × 20

⇒ V = 22 × (14 ÷ 7) × 14 × 20

⇒ V = 22 × 2 × 14 × 20

⇒ V = 44 × 280

⇒ V = 12320 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 12320 cm³.**

**__Additional Information__**

Curved Surface Area of Cylinder

The area of the curved part of the cylinder is given by CSA = 2πrh.

Total Surface Area of Cylinder

The sum of the areas of the curved surface and the two circular bases: TSA = 2πr(h + r).

Volume Conversion

1 cm³ = 1 mL and 1000 cm³ = 1 Liter.</p
